why: A Critical Parent command that invalidates the customer's feelings; turns frustration into anger.
instead: I realize this whole thing has been frustrating for you.

phrase: That's our policy. / I can't do that.
why: Hides behind rules, removes the customer's autonomy, invites escalation.
instead: While I can't do X, what I can do is Y.

phrase: That's not my responsibility. / I don't know.
why: Projects incompetence and leaves the customer feeling unsupported.
instead: Let me find that out for you. Here's what I'll do next.

why: Removes the human connection without consent; creates anxiety about how long and why.
instead: May I place you on a brief hold for about two minutes while I check your account?

why: Attacks the customer's competence and turns problem-solving into a battle of egos.
instead: Let me make sure I explained that clearly.

why: Sounds robotic and generic; "any" implies you don't understand their specific pain.
instead: I'm sorry your order arrived late. I know you were counting on it.
